lines.text: The scariest movie ever made... was inspired by a real exorcism. And then the set started burning.
1949. A fourteen year old boy from Maryland, known only as Roland Doe.
His family said it started after he played with a Ouija board. Scratching inside the walls. A bed that shook on its own.
Jesuit priests took him to St. Louis, to the Alexian Brothers Hospital. Reports say they performed dozens of exorcisms on him.
A Georgetown student named William Peter Blatty heard the story. Twenty years later, he turned it into a novel.
In 1973 it became The Exorcist. And during filming... things started going wrong.
A fire destroyed most of the set. Crew members said the one room left untouched... was the possessed girl's bedroom.
A priest was brought in to bless the set.
Actor Jack MacGowran, whose character dies in the film, died before it was released. So did Vasiliki Maliaros, who played the priest's mother.
Some reports later linked nine deaths to the production.
Skeptics say long, dangerous shoots always have accidents. But the cast still talks about that set.
Would you watch it alone tonight? Sleep tight, partner.
